L0@P0: DIRECTIVE 2026-45
L1@P0: August 25, 2026
L2@P0: To: All County Boards of Elections
L3@P0: Board Members, Directors, and Deputy Directors
L4@P0: Re: Form of the Official Ballot for the November 3, 2026, General Election
L5@P0: SUMMARY
L6@P0: This Directive provides the certified forms of the official ballots to be used in the
L7@P0: November 3, 2026, General Election. Each board of elections must thoroughly and
L8@P0: promptly check every detail of its ballots from the creation of the ballot to submitting
L9@P0: the ballot files to the printer to be produced and fully comply with Chapter 5 of the
L10@P0: EOM. Ultimately, the responsibility for ensuring the ballot is correct rests with the board
L11@P0: members, as indicated by their signatures. A board member’s signature has legal
L12@P0: significance and indicates the board member is accepting full responsibility and
L13@P0: ownership of ensuring the accuracy of the ballot. The board must develop, maintain,
L14@P0: and practice policies and procedures to ensure this responsibility is met at all levels. This
L15@P0: is a basic and essential function of the board.
L16@P0: INSTRUCTIONS
L17@P0: Please note that, in lieu of issuing a separate Directive with specific details covering
L18@P0: ballot layout, proofing, and quantities, the Secretary of State’s office is issuing only this
L19@P0: Directive, which must be used in conjunction with Chapter 5 (Ballots) of the Election
L20@P0: Official Manual (EOM) when preparing ballots for this election. Chapter 5 of the EOM
L21@P0: provides specific instructions on the following subjects:
L22@P0: • ballot format
L23@P0: • voter instructions
L24@P0: • ballot stubs
L25@P0: • candidate ballots (names, restrictions, political party, rotation, etc.)
L26@P0: • questions and issues ballots
L27@P0: • ballot proofs
L28@P0: • overlaps
L29@P0-1: • bid requirementsOffice of the Ohio Secretary of State 2 | page
L30@P1: • ballot quantities
L31@P1: • logic and accuracy testing
L32@P1: • public testing
L33@P1: I. VERIFYING DISTRICT RELATIONSHIPS
L34@P1: Before programming any aspect of the central tabulating system for the November
L35@P1: 3, 2026, General Election, boards of elections must verify the accuracy of district
L36@P1: relationships in the central tabulating system against the county’s voter registration
L37@P1: system. This is to ensure that each voter receives the correct ballot style (that is, the
L38@P1: correct combination of candidate contests and ballot questions and issues) based
L39@P1: upon that voter’s residential address.
L40@P1: As a part of the review for accuracy of district relationships between the county’s
L41@P1: voter registration system and its tabulating system, the board must ensure the
L42@P1: following by Wednesday, September 16, 2026:
L43@P1: A. The Secretary of State’s precinct codes (three alphabet letters) are accurate
L44@P1: in the tabulating system and, if appropriate, the county’s voter registration
L45@P1: system; and
L46@P1: B. The precinct names correspond between the two systems.
L47@P1: Note: It is imperative that a board of elections upload to the statewide voter
L48@P1: registration database (SWVRD) any changes to district relationships
L49@P1: (including wards and precincts) that have been made locally in the
L50@P1: county’s voter registration system (VRS). Using the report, which will be
L51@P1: provided by Allison Scott on Friday, September 11, 2026, each board
L52@P1: must review the report to ensure that all Secretary of State Precinct ID
L53@P1: Codes provided on the report match the board’s voter registration
L54@P1: system. Boards will have until Wednesday, September 16, 2026, to return
L55@P1: the reviewed report, noting any changes.
L56@P1: In addition, the board must verify at least one voter record for each precinct in the
L57@P1: SWVRD against the county’s VRS to ensure accuracy.
L58@P1: II. OFFICIAL BALLOT FORMS
L59@P1: The certified ballot form accompanying this directive is for offices to be elected at
L60@P1: the November 3, 2026, General Election. The ballot form contains the correct title for
L61@P1-2: each office, how that title should appear on your county’s ballot, and the order in Office of the Ohio Secretary of State 3 | page
L62@P2: which offices must appear on the ballot for all voting systems. The ballot form also
L63@P2: contains the name of each statewide candidate exactly as the candidate’s name must
L64@P2: appear on all ballots for all voting systems.
L65@P2: The names of all candidates who have not withdrawn pursuant to R.C. 3513.30 must
L66@P2: be arranged, rotated, and printed upon the ballot in accordance with the provisions
L67@P2: of Ohio Revised Code Chapters 3505, 3506, and 3513, and Chapter 5 of the EOM.
L68@P2: III. ORDER OF OFFICES FOR ALL BALLOTS1
L69@P2: A. The order of offices for ballots shall be as follows:
L70@P2: • Governor and Lieutenant Governor
L71@P2: • Attorney General
L72@P2: • Auditor of State
L73@P2: • Secretary of State
L74@P2: • Treasurer of State
L75@P2: • Justice of the Supreme Court (Full term commencing 1/1/2027)
L76@P2: • Justice of the Supreme Court (Full term commencing 1/2/2027)
L77@P2: • U.S. Senator (Unexpired term ending 1/3/2029)
L78@P2: • Representative to Congress
L79@P2: • State Senator
L80@P2: • State Representative
L81@P2: • Judge of the Court of Appeals
L82@P2: • Judge of the Court of Common Pleas
L83@P2: • County Court Judge
L84@P2: • County Commissioner
L85@P2: • County Auditor
L86@P2: B. Write-In Vote Blank Spaces
L87@P2: A write-in space must be provided on the ballot for every office for which the
L88@P2: board of elections or Secretary of State received a valid declaration of intent to
L89@P2: be a write-in candidate.2 If there is both a full and an unexpired term for the
L90@P2: same office, place the full term first, followed by the unexpired term.
L91@P2-3: 1 R.C. 3505.03(C); R.C. 3505.04. 2 R.C. 3513.041.Office of the Ohio Secretary of State 4 | page
L92@P3: Below is the list of valid write-in candidates for the November 3, 2026, General
L93@P3: Election.
L94@P3: i. Governor and Lieutenant Governor
L95@P3: • Timothy Grady and Andrea Neutzling
L96@P3: • Heather Hill and Patrick Manley
L97@P3: • Renea Turner and Jalen Turner
L98@P3: • Ron Ula and Michael C. Lehnerd
L99@P3: ii. U.S. Senator
L100@P3: • Stephen Faris
L101@P3: • Anthony Holliman
L102@P3: • Timothy Telymonde
L103@P3: IV. OFFICIAL QUESTIONS AND ISSUES BALLOT
L104@P3: Offices for which candidates may be nominated or elected are presented on the
L105@P3: ballot first, followed by the questions and issues. The Official Questions and Issues
L106@P3: Ballot must be used for all voting systems. The attached ballot form contains
L107@P3: examples of some of the local questions and issues that may appear on the ballot in
L108@P3: your county. Not every category or type of question/issue will appear on every ballot
L109@P3: in every county, so please apply as much of the form as is appropriate to the ballots
L110@P3: in your county.
L111@P3: Additional instructions on headings, ballot language, and percentage of votes can be
L112@P3: found in Chapter 5 of the EOM.
L113@P3: Please note that Statewide Issue 3 will appear on the November 3, 2026, ballot.
L114@P3: Questions and issues must be grouped together in the following political subdivision
L115@P3: order for elections held in 2026:
L116@P3: 3
L117@P3: A. State
L118@P3: B. School and Other Districts
L119@P3: C. County
L120@P3: D. Municipal
L121@P3: E. Township
L122@P3-4: 3 R.C. 3505.06(B); Ohio Ballot Question and Issues Handbook, pg. 9.Office of the Ohio Secretary of State 5 | page
L123@P4: Each board of elections may determine the specific order in which the
L124@P4: questions/issues within each group are placed on the ballot in that county4
L125@P4: ; however,
L126@P4: a board should adopt a method for doing so (for example, ordered alphabetically or
L127@P4: by date filed, etc.). Absentee ballots must contain identical ordering of issues within
L128@P4: groups to regular ballots.
L129@P4: Please review the appropriate sections of the Ohio Revised Code, local charter (if
L130@P4: applicable), and the Ohio Ballot Questions and Issues Handbook for ballot language
L131@P4: and formats that are not on the attached Official Questions and Issues Ballot.
L132@P4: V. ABSENTEE BALLOTS5
L133@P4: Each board of elections must have absentee ballots printed and ready for use by
L134@P4: Friday, September 18, 2026 (46 days before the November 3, 2026 General Election),
L135@P4: for Uniformed and Overseas Citizens Absentee Voting Act (UOCAVA) voters, and by
L136@P4: October 6, 2026, for regular (non-UOCAVA) absentee voters.
L137@P4: A copy of each absentee ballot (candidates and questions and issues) must be sent
L138@P4: to the Secretary of State’s office at least 47 days before the election, by Thursday,
L139@P4: September 17, 2026. Absentee ballots must be uploaded to the SharePoint site.

L190@P6: VII. CANDIDATES FOR OTHER DISTRICT OFFICE (for example, Congress,
L191@P6: Court of Appeals Judge, State Senate, and State Representative)
